approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from previously evaluated molecules. It retains a bounded population by score, draws breeding parents from preferred score bands, and generates a surplus pool through connected-fragment crossover or ordinary one-parent mutation walks. A successful crossover has a separate 35% chance of one finishing mutation before validity and duplicate checks. The Parent already excludes the direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen positional exchange. Its Gaussian process learns from the complete chronological archive of accepted task-local scores, using counts of local molecular environments and generalized Tanimoto similarity. Correlated posterior draws choose the molecules to evaluate; accepted offspring update both the model archive and the score-ranked breeding population.
approach.novelty: Test the interaction between the already evaluated two-cut ring construction and removal of crossover finishing. Reuse the ring construction exactly: when both actual parents support it, it can join complete components cut from two parental rings at two endpoints under the original uniform choices. Disable the finishing branch for every successful crossover while retaining its random draw. This sends the immediate recombinants to ordinary admission without another edit at that boundary. The earlier ring-only sibling built and evaluated new rings but lost score; some of its finished products also lost the new ring pattern. Neither that result nor earlier donor-conditioning siblings tested this joint treatment. The concurrent finishing-only control completes the four-treatment comparison needed to distinguish an interaction from the general effect of removing finishing. Structural persistence may help search, but greater persistence alone cannot establish an endpoint gain.

observed_bottleneck: The targeted Parent boundary is the extra mutation between a successful crossover and ordinary pool admission; its conditional effect on a newly constructed ring has not been isolated. The actual n-62daf219c70a per-seed summary.json and run.log files show a complete successful current-profile panel, macro mean 0.5956696497334577 and population SD 0.02659287062806747. Its source has a separate post_crossover_mutation_probability=0.35 gate, while ordinary one-parent continuation has its own schedule. Current removal controls support retaining whole crossover (n-767d2ce08797, paired mean -0.054937284705486644) and ordinary continuation (n-dbee08307e86, -0.02686763734135833); neither isolates finishing; the ordinary-continuation control is scoped to the floor-one schedule. The exact ring-only n-870ed6964d46 panel is also complete, mean 0.5506233616093282, SD 0.04582641958080816, paired mean -0.04504628812412936 and seed deltas [-0.014403656031368062, -0.020054909582571057, -0.10068029875844897]. Ten task-seed endpoints fall, two rise and three tie. Its full activation audit records 5498 selected ring constructions on 10982 jointly eligible crossover opportunities, 5496 below-limit raw constructions satisfying the two-attachment invariants, and 179 accepted noncopy descendants. The newly constructed typed cycle embeds in all 124 pure noncopy evaluations but only 43 of 55 finished noncopies; both full component patterns embed in 124/124 versus 27/55. These adaptively selected cohorts do not estimate a finishing effect. Six task-seed cells evaluate no ring-mode descendant. Ninety-six accepted noncopy descendants later breed, and overall local parent beats increase from 629 to 652 despite weaker absolute parent/offspring scores and worse endpoints. Thus the specific unresolved limitation is whether the retained finishing boundary disrupts the useful transmission of this exact construction, not whether raw ring generation can execute. The failed donor-conditioning n-eb61315a5619 and copy-exclusion n-bddb1dbe8e32 variants retain their negative complete effects (-0.020270634588430703 and -0.10265273096567833); more distinct or parent-beating recombinants did not rescue them. No missing Parent source, summary, run log or indexed trajectory was found.
hypothesis: Combine the exact optional two-cut ring-segment crossover of n-870ed6964d46 with removal of post-crossover finishing on code Parent n-62daf219c70a: set only post_crossover_mutation_probability from 0.35 to 0.0 while retaining its existing random draw after every successful ordinary or ring-mode crossover.

finding_summary.headline: Intact ring products reached breeding; a positive but uneven interaction did not recover the Anchor score
finding_summary.insights:
Finishing is a real conditional boundary for this exact construction: the four matched conditions show that its total effect changes when ring mode is present. Correct construction, intact evaluated rings and later breeding rule out a globally broken delivery mechanism, but they do not restore the required endpoint performance. The apparent benefit is concentrated in seed 2, especially docking, and the ring-without-finishing contrast itself is negative in two of three seed macros. Those shared controls are dependent evidence, so the positive mean interaction does not establish a reliable general benefit or independent component replication.

Structural preservation alone is insufficient as an explanation. All three median-2 endpoints improve despite no evaluated ring-mode descendant, and one zaleplon gain occurs with no selected ring construction at all. Eligible mode draws, unselected pool competitors and changed adaptive histories can still change those searches. The joint run produces more local best-parent wins overall (768 versus 629), but mean generating-parent score falls from 0.470456 to 0.403872, mean offspring score from 0.385256 to 0.341961, and the average positive incumbent step from 0.022510 to 0.017312. That separates frequent small local gains from stronger final search.

The chemistry further limits the claim. Ring-rich aromatic and nitrogen/carbonyl families coexist with reactive attachments, difficult bridges or small-ring unsaturation and unresolved stereochemistry. Distinct typed and generic cores fall even as ring-only graph diversity rises; nearby high-scoring conventional examples show that the questionable attachments are not universally needed. Preserving a typed cycle therefore proves neither useful geometry nor feasible synthesis. The present evidence answers the fixed joint contribution question and rejects its separate performance prediction. Which preserved products, lost finishing products, random-stream changes or later feedback paths explain the interaction remains open; no unselected alternative received a score, and no chemical mediation claim follows.
finding_summary.results:
All 35,061 successful crossovers retained their original gate draw and skipped finishing; 12,487 draws fell below the former 35% threshold. Ring mode made 5,283 valid two-attachment products. All 169 evaluated noncopy descendants retained the new typed cycle and both selected component patterns, versus 167 of 179 and 151 of 179 in the ring-only treatment. The evaluated noncopy count nevertheless fell from 179 to 169. All 161 nonterminal ring births entered the next model fit, 103 later bred, 41 beat their best parent and 12 improved the incumbent. Eight terminal births were censored; nine task/seed cells evaluated no ring descendant.

The complete four-condition comparison gives a mean interaction of +0.047285, with seed interactions -0.004750, +0.009258 and +0.137346 (population SD 0.063939). Removing finishing improves the ring-only mean by +0.011042, while removing it without ring mode lowers the mean by -0.036243. This is a heterogeneous interaction: ten task/seed interactions are positive, three negative and two unchanged. The joint mean remains 0.561665 versus the Anchor’s 0.595670, a loss of -0.034004 against the required +0.002 gain. Six endpoints improve and nine decline; seed macro changes are -0.078161, +0.010125 and -0.033978. Seed population SD falls from 0.026593 to 0.010338 around the lower mean.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic and nitrogen-carbonyl families retain reactive attachments, difficult ring geometry and unresolved stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: Assessed n-6e3c92b5dcd0 against published code Parent n-62daf219c70a using all supplied Search trajectories. All 15 Child and 15 Parent paths exist and were read in full; each has 300 consecutive finite-score observations, comprising 10 initial records and 290 accepted optimizer proposals. The complete Child digest is reproduced exactly, all summary endpoints agree, and every same-seed initial molecular identity and score agrees. Both context.comparison.child_complete and paired_complete are true; no supplied path, task or matched Parent comparison is missing. All 15 Child molecular identity/score trajectories differ from Parent. The observations concern accepted evaluated proposals; unselected pool graphs have no labels here. The digest final_molecules are the pooled tail of seed 2, not each seed's incumbent, and score_span includes initial records. Full trajectories supply the other seed leaders and late counterexamples. The registered scope is the joint intervention in n-6e3c92b5dcd0. Indexed original chemistry in n-c55c3d520a2c, its published baseline recurrence in n-62daf219c70a, and the existing ring-only comparator n-870ed6964d46 were read through context.evidence_index. The immutable request lists the finishing-only treatment as pending; it supplies no complete current four-treatment comparison. Unfinished concurrent controls and unrelated rank controls are not completed evidence for that missing cell. The output associations below establish neither activation, interaction, component contribution nor chemical mediation. Historical gaps keep their original Development-profile origin and current-profile recurrence; their effects are not pooled across those conditions. Across the 4,350 accepted Child proposals, heavy-atom counts span 2-120, median 30, versus Parent 1-107, median 28. There are 4,283 Child molecules with perceived rings and 4,248 with aromatic atoms. The taskwise digest ring-closure-string rates are 0.9782-0.9908, and aromatic-string rates 0.9529-0.9885: molecule-level text incidences, not ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. The output includes compact indole/benzimidazole-like amides, unsaturated benzofused small rings, linked and densely bridged azaheterocycles, aryl-containing cyclic and flexible amines, medium nitrogen/carbonyl rings, and fluorinated small rings attached to fused nitrogen diones. Nonaromatic rings occur in 3,214 Child proposals versus 2,757 Parent proposals; saturated rings occur in 1,257 versus 1,266. Seven Child proposals have a perceived ring of at least 12 atoms, all in the nitrogen/carbonyl stream, with a maximum of 15; the Parent has one such proposal elsewhere. Ring access is already substantial. Local chemistry remains uneven. Molecule-level Child counts are 978 with N-halogen, 479 with O-halogen, 112 with O-O and 4 with halogen-halogen bonds. Their overlapping union is 1,436 versus Parent 1,490; this modest aggregate reduction masks increases in some streams and does not establish uniformly better chemistry. High-scoring examples without any of those bonds are real counterexamples, while an unusual neutral S=C/S-N/S-aryl environment shows that this limited screen is incomplete. RDKit finds potential tetrahedral centres in 2,132 Child proposals versus 2,408 Parent proposals; all are unassigned. Explicit atom chirality, double-bond stereochemistry and formal charge are absent in both streams. Neutral aliphatic amines are present, so absence of charge notation is not absence of basic centres. Structural diversity is moderate across seeds and tasks but narrower among leaders within a seed. Child/Parent distinct typed Murcko cores are 1,757/1,851, generic Murcko cores 1,084/1,118, and generic ring-only graphs 656/631. Those disagreeing coverage measures cannot certify chemical independence or useful exploration. Synthetic plausibility is questionable and drug-likeness weak overall because recognizable functional groups coexist with reactive attachments, unusual valence, difficult bridges and small-ring unsaturation. Ordinary amides, saturated small rings and cyclic amines remain genuine plausible substructures; they should not be conflated with the specific liabilities. No conformation, synthesis, stability, protonation or biological validation is supplied by these records. Audit definitions and full measurements are in .slots/round-0023-slot-1/molecular/audit.json, with a reproducible audit.py and source hashes. RDKit 2023.09.6 parsed all 9,000 Child/Parent rows. Rings refer to perceived atom rings and may include symmetry-related cycles; they are not independent ring-construction events. Typed cores use GetScaffoldForMol; generic cores use MakeScaffoldGeneric, with stereo omitted and one <acyclic> sentinel for an empty scaffold. The separate generic ring-only graph retains only ring bonds and incident atoms, removes linkers and exocyclic atoms, and makes retained atoms carbon and bonds single, retaining disconnected multiplicity. The ten highest existing scores per cell define only a descriptive chemistry stratum. Motif counts denote bond presence, not a complete reactivity or safety model. Structural similarity and retained scaffold labels establish neither pedigree ancestry nor literal source-atom conservation.

per_task.generated_character: Accepted proposals span 2-48 heavy atoms, median 24, and 851/870 have both perceived rings and aromatic atoms. Seed 0's 25-heavy-atom leader at evaluation 228 contains an N-hydroxy indole-like fused aromatic region, an N-fluoro amide linked to pyridyl, methyl groups and an allenyl substituent. Its nearby vinyl/phenyl analogue retains the same reactive N-F and N-O environments, while another relative has hydrogen-bearing sulfur in a cumulated C=C=S segment. Seed 1's 25-heavy-atom leader is a vinyl/methyl/chloromethyl benzimidazole-like N-methyl anilide, with ordinary carbon-bound aryl chlorine and no N-halogen bond. Seed 2's 25-heavy-atom leader instead has a benzofused unsaturated four-membered carbocycle, hydroxymethyl, N-fluoro amide and N-chlorinated hydrazine-like substitution on its anilide. These are compact aromatic frameworks, but familiar size and amide functionality coexist with questionable local chemistry or ring geometry. Parent leaders occupy related aromatic families: an amino-cumulene/N-chloro heterocycle, an N-hydroxy amide with N-fluorinated indole nitrogen, and an N-chloro indole vicinal diketone. The Child therefore changes functional placement and ring connectivity without uniformly removing the inherited liabilities. Generic-core coverage is 86 versus Parent 124; this is no claim of absent ring access.
liabilities: N-F amide, N-O heterocycle and N-chlorinated nitrogen groups are distinct from ordinary carbon-bound fluorine or chlorine. N-halogen bonds occur in 410/870 proposals versus Parent 445/870, so the issue recurs despite a lower count.
The sulfur-containing cumulated segment combines unusual valence and explicit sulfur hydrogen. The seed-2 benzofused unsaturated four-membered ring adds a separate ring-geometry concern.
The N-halogen-free seed-1 leader still bears a chloromethyl group; escaping the limited alert screen is not a demonstration of overall stability or synthetic ease.
missing_features: Stable local alternatives expressing the favorable compact aromatic/carbonyl organization are not consistently developed at the leading scores; conventional N-H and N-methyl amides already demonstrate that the generator can produce such chemistry.

The benzofused unsaturated four-membered arrangement lacks demonstrated geometric feasibility, while the allenyl and unusual sulfur variants lack measured stability. The scores do not identify a required reactive bond.

Chemically independent plausible alternatives to each seed's close aromatic family remain uneven. No exact absent target-specific pharmacophore, or score benefit from added donors or rings, can be inferred from these examples.

per_task.generated_character: Accepted proposals span 2-120 heavy atoms, median 36, with 858/870 carrying rings and aromatic atoms. Mean size is 44.58 heavy atoms versus Parent 33.28. Seed 0's 29-heavy-atom leader joins densely fused/bridged azaheterocyclic regions through a thioamide and carries N-methyl groups, carbon-bound fluorine and O-Br. RDKit perceives overlapping five-, six- and seven-membered cycles in this highly cross-linked graph; their multiplicity does not demonstrate accessible geometry. Seed 1's 38-heavy-atom leader is quite different: two substituted six-membered aromatic rings connected through a benzylamino segment, with methoxy/ethoxy/enol-ether groups and a fluoro-imine/alkenyl-thioether chain. Its shorter 35-heavy-atom relative has the same score. Seed 2's 36-heavy-atom leader links dense nitrogen-rich carbonyl/thione systems, with N-N connectivity and a partly saturated ring segment. Larger multi-core elaborations also occur. The Parent's highest seed-0 family is a compact linked aza-aromatic/carbonyl-thione assembly; the Child does not reproduce that favorable chemical organization at its higher Parent score. Other Parent seeds have different aryl-ether/azaheterocycle or peroxide-bearing linked-ring families. These are substantial molecules, not a lack of rings or functional groups, but synthetic plausibility is weakened by difficult junctions and reactive peripheral bonds.
liabilities: O-halogen bonds occur in 320/870 proposals versus Parent 89/870. Peroxide incidence falls to 70/870 from 218/870, but the limited alert union rises to 371/870 from 304/870; chemical changes are mixed.

The flexible leading family contains an imidoyl-fluoride-like N=C(F) environment and enol-ether/thioether segments. A near-leading peroxide variant at seed 1 evaluation 281 retains 0.6175157563025211. These environments require distinct stability assessments.

Crowded nitrogen-rich fused and bridged carbonyl/thione systems, long flexible substituents and oversized multi-core products present different synthetic problems. An alert-free record does not resolve these geometry and complexity concerns.
missing_features: More reliable access to the favorable compact linked heterocyclic organization seen in the Parent is absent from these Child leaders; simply adding rings, side-chain atoms or another heterocyclic region does not recover that score.

The dense azaheterocyclic junctions lack demonstrated accessible geometry and a plausible route, while stable peripheral alternatives are only partly explored. High-scoring O-halogen-free relatives are a real counterexample to a universal reactive-bond requirement.

The seed-1 family lacks chemical independence among its leading examples even though its substituents vary. The record does not expose an exact missing pharmacophore or show that stability itself is rewarded by the objective.

The Child's leading graphs do not repeat that strongest Parent geometry, but cyclic cumulated bonds remain elsewhere: digest incidence is 0.1 versus Parent 0.0517. liabilities: N-halogen bonds occur in 401/870 proposals versus Parent 476/870. Both N-F and N-S/N-N environments must be distinguished from ordinary carbon-bound fluorine, and N-halogen-free examples still retain other possible liabilities.

Cyclopropene, hydroxycyclobutene and cyclic-cumulene contexts impose different strain and reactivity questions. A saturated small ring is not equivalent to cumulated double bonds constrained within a small ring.

Large duplicated-core products can retain many favorable-looking atom types while losing the compact arrangement associated with reward. No score, aromatic flag or ring-preservation observation demonstrates a physical conformer, feasible synthesis or biological activity.
missing_features: The output does not consistently combine its compact fluorinated nitrogen/carbonyl organization with conventional stable attachments and defined small-ring geometry. Saturated fluorocyclopropyl and fluorocyclobutyl examples already show partial access to more conventional motifs.

Stereochemical identities of the substituted small rings and saturated junctions are unspecified; 594/870 proposals have potential tetrahedral centres. Tautomeric and conformational identities of imino, enolic and aromatic-labelled regions also remain unresolved.

Stable alternatives retaining the leading functional context are not established at the highest observed scores. The data do not identify an exact missing target pharmacophore or a universal benefit from adding more fluorine, amines or carbonyls.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The shared initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.0020944534688323298. Seed 1's fluorocyclopropyl leader reaches 0.5570560592089596 versus 0.4917876364690907 for its fluorocyclobutenyl relative at evaluation 289. This is a direct observed counterexample to the idea that more ring unsaturation is always rewarded. In seed 2, the difluorocyclobutyl variant at evaluation 252 scores 0.46197234675236604 and the additional carbon-bound-fluorine variant at evaluation 273 scores 0.5362288282440508. An N-methyl, N-halogen-free cyclobutenyl analogue at evaluation 200 reaches 0.4092437126034247, so N-F is not a universal prerequisite for appreciable score. The final N-S-containing small-ring variant at evaluation 300 falls to 0.1733777878594261. Seed 0's cyclopropene/imino leader scores 0.40865183215460454. At the low end, the 52-heavy-atom doubled carbonyl/aldehyde system at seed 2 evaluation 198 scores 1.874678035689159e-24, the 52-heavy-atom cyclic-cumulene multi-core structure at evaluation 55 scores 1.0060533870051351e-23, and FF at seed 1 evaluation 159 scores 4.97400031457045e-24. Reward in this record depends on compact functional and fluorination context, not fluorine count, duplicated cores or extreme size. These are structural associations and supplied objective values, not evidence that reactive bonds or strained rings are needed. Recorded Child/Parent final Top-1 values are seed 0: 0.408651832155/0.651021190703, difference -0.242369358548; seed 1: 0.557056059209/0.487005730568, difference +0.0700503286411; seed 2: 0.536228828244/0.720885366842, difference -0.184656538598. These are the existing matched observations, not new scores or an attribution of the chemistry to either component.

Among 4,350 accepted proposals, 978 contain N-halogen, 479 O-halogen, 112 O-O and 4 halogen-halogen bonds; their overlapping union is 1,436 versus Parent 1,490. transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional local bond environments while modifying otherwise useful molecular frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need context-sensitive alternatives distinguishing conventional carbon-bound halogens, amines and ethers from reactive heteroatom attachments and unusual valence environments, while preserving relationships supported by its accepted local feedback. The evidence motivates chemical capability, not a claim that a universal exclusion filter improves score or that either component caused the attachments.

There are 4,283 ring-containing proposals and 656 generic ring-only graphs, versus Parent 4,221 and 631. Seven proposals contain a perceived ring of at least 12 atoms, with a maximum of 15. Leaders and relatives include an unsaturated benzofused four-membered ring, dense bridged azaheterocycles, large aromatic-labelled nitrogen circuits and small-ring cumulenes. Saturated fluorocyclopropyl and fluorocyclobutyl examples are important counterexamples; an observed saturated small-ring variant scores above its unsaturated relative. The gap is therefore not inability to produce rings or ordinary small saturated rings.
transferable_gaps.gap: Rich ring construction is not consistently accompanied by credible unsaturation, bridge connectivity and functional context.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring transformations would need sensitivity to bond geometry, bridge connectivity, ring size and local functional arrangement, with credible alternative topologies evaluated through task-local feedback. Perceived ring count or a retained typed cycle cannot establish synthesis, literal atom provenance or useful conformation. Ring-specific restrictions or expansions have no demonstrated score benefit from this association alone.

transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not specify stereochemical identity after generating potentially stereogenic saturated and bridged environments.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Representation and transformations would need to preserve or resolve stereochemical identity where chemically appropriate, distinguishing stable stereocentres from achiral or configurationally unstable environments. Historical and current effects are not pooled, and the unfinished parallel control does not supply component attribution. The Child has 72 accepted proposals with at most five heavy atoms versus Parent 123, yet late tiny molecules still lie near their observed score floors. At the other extreme, Child size reaches 120 heavy atoms versus Parent 107. A leading linked-ring family has 35- and 38-heavy-atom variants with the same recorded score, while a 45-heavy-atom relative is slightly lower. A 53-heavy-atom multi-core relative is below a 36-heavy-atom leader; a 52-heavy-atom doubled fluorinated/carbonyl system lies near the floor. These are conditional context failures, not evidence for a universal desired size.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator still loses useful functional context in tiny fragments while also emitting oversized or unnecessarily elaborate relatives.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Use accepted task-local feedback to support context-preserving simplification, fragmentation and recombination, retaining the functional arrangement that made related molecules informative. Neither a fixed minimum size nor automatic growth follows from these examples. Distinct identity and sanitation cannot separate useful simplification from loss of the entire molecular context.

Child/Parent whole-panel distinct typed cores are 1,757/1,851, generic cores 1,084/1,118 and generic ring-only graphs 656/631 under one acyclic sentinel. transferable_gaps.gap: Chemically independent plausible alternatives to the leading frameworks remain uneven despite substantial molecular and ring-graph diversity.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need chemically credible alternative frameworks preserving the functional relationships supported by its own accepted observations. Track structural coverage, subsequent evaluated usefulness and plausibility separately. Maximizing core counts, sharing a founder or retaining a ring does not prove productive exploration, literal atom conservation or either component's contribution.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
